title: Pokkén Tournament
subtitle: Pokémon fight at the player’s command
summary: Pokkén Tournament is Bandai Namco's action fighting game built around Pokémon, first released in Japanese arcades on 16 July 2015.
body: Pokkén Tournament is Bandai Namco's action fighting game built around Pokémon, first released in Japanese arcades on 16 July 2015. Two players directly control individual creatures in battles that move between a free-roaming arena and a closer side-on confrontation. Familiar Pokémon attacks become actions to perform and time, giving the series' characters another kind of encounter. The player must read distance, an opponent's intentions and the opportunities attached to the current phase rather than issue commands to a larger party.

Field Phase allows movement around the arena, while Duel Phase concentrates the fighters into a more conventional head-to-head space. The shift changes which movements and attacks are useful. A Synergy Gauge builds towards stronger techniques and transformations, while Support Pokémon provide additional effects to help shape an exchange. The arcade machine uses a console-style controller rather than a traditional stick, reflecting the aim of making the fighting approachable. Its systems offer recognizable Pokémon powers inside a contest governed by immediate control and positioning.

The worldwide Wii U edition arrived on 18 March 2016, bringing the arcade design home with online competition and further content. A Shadow Mewtwo amiibo card accompanied early copies, and the expanded Pokkén Tournament DX followed on Switch in 2017. Producers Katsuhiro Harada and Masaaki Hoshino brought fighting-game experience to the collaboration, with Haruki Suzaki directing. The result gives each Pokémon a physical presence in the match, using changes of phase to connect an open arena encounter to the concentrated timing of a traditional fighting game.
